title: JANUS Engine — Howl's Moving Castle RUN-004, literature-calibrated direct-gill PEMFC
purpose: Repeat the self-drive calculation using measured and target artificial-gill/PEMFC performance reported by Merckelbach & Georgopanos (2025), while retaining the JANUS R0A1 membrane crown as the scale envelope and removing the full O2/N2/LOX processing burden from the direct mode.

source_data.target_inference_basis: Authors report measured 1.5-2.5 umol/s as roughly 6-10 times below target; both endpoints imply a target near 15 umol/s for the 3 m2 module.

janus_geometry_carried_from_R0A1.architecture: rotating Axle plus stationary high-area gill crown

R0A1_hydraulic_reference.flow_regime_note: R0A1 straight-channel screen was laminar; RUN-004 scales hydraulic power approximately with Q^2 only as a low-flow screening relation.

case_A_measured_prototype_flux_scaled_to.interpretation: The published desktop prototype flux is experimentally real but too low, when linearly scaled to 423.5 m2, to pay a 100 W shared overhead. The water-pumping bill at the correspondingly lower throughput is tiny; the deficit is dominated by fixed/gas-side auxiliaries rather than hydraulic power.

case_B_paper_target_flux_scaled_to_JANUS.interpretation: At the paper's intended module-level transfer rate, the JANUS crown no longer needs the old 0.4 g/s oxygen target to become self-driving. A roughly 0.068 g/s O2 stream already yields about 254 W gross electrical power, leaving about 147 W after the current fixed and water-side screening loads, before gas recirculation/hydrogen-feed/thermal auxiliaries are charged.

break_even_transport_for_423p53m2.design_meaning: RUN-004 does not require the full paper target to cross zero if gas-side auxiliaries are controlled. With the current 100 W shared overhead and no additional gas-loop penalty, about 40% of the paper target flux is mathematically enough.

old_0p4g_s_target_reassessment.conclusion: The previous 0.4 g/s target is too aggressive for a first direct-gill PEMFC self-drive demonstration at current literature-calibrated membrane transport. RUN-004 therefore changes the optimization objective from hitting 0.4 g/s to crossing P_net=0 at the lowest realizable oxygen flux and auxiliary burden.

comparison_to_RUN003_full_VRU_AKS.direct_mode_effect: Bulk gas separation, N2 service and LOX are not required for first ignition; this removes a major auxiliary block but replaces it with an explicit recirculating cathode-gas loop whose power must be measured.
comparison_to_RUN003_full_VRU_AKS.strategic_result: MODE_A_DIRECT_GILL_PEMFC is now the preferred first-self-drive path; MODE_B_VRU_AKS remains the richer process-integration architecture for later scaling and storage functions.

dominant_unknowns_after_RUN004: actual O2 flux of a JANUS membrane cassette under controlled water velocity and internal pO2
gas recirculation blower power required to maintain the PEMFC loop
hydrogen storage/feed parasitic power and chosen fuel-cell stack efficiency
long-duration membrane fouling and flux recovery
scale-up maldistribution inside the annular crown

run_verdict.main_discovery: Only about 0.027 g/s O2 and 0.064 mg m-2 s-1 membrane flux are required to beat the current 100 W fixed overhead in the direct PEMFC screen; the first self-drive target can be much smaller than 0.4 g/s.

next_gate: R0A2_SMALL_CASSETTE_TRANSPORT_CALIBRATION + R2B1_GAS_LOOP_PARASITIC_GATE: measure J_O2(v_water,pO2_internal), DeltaP/Q and blower power on a small closed recirculating cathode loop. Re-run with measured JANUS values; do not scale to the full 423.5 m2 crown until the small cassette closes O2 and energy balances.
